content.text: No restraint on Customer exists anywhere; §12.3 expressly negates one, and §12.4's restraint binds Vendor (which benefits us).

input.quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement meets the preferred position: §12.3 expressly confirms that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, or conducting business in any field or territory, and that Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. The only competition restraint (§12.4) binds Vendor for our benefit, so it is not flagged. Section 2.1 also confirms no minimum purchase commitment, and the §13.4 restrictions (reverse engineering, interference, unlawful use) are ordinary use rules, not field-of-use or non-compete restraints. No sections elsewhere (§§2, 13, 14, 25, 26, 30) impose any restraint on our lines of business.

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
mappings.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
